title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: all Group personnel
tiers.description: All directors, senior executives, employees, agents, contractors and consultants of the Company and its related bodies corporate. Subject to the insider trading prohibition (section 2) and the general trading rules in section 3 (no margin lending, no short-term/speculative trading, no short selling).

tiers.name: Designated Personnel
tiers.description: All directors and senior executives of the Group, plus any other persons identified by the Board or the Company Secretary from time to time. Subject to Prohibited Periods, exceptional-circumstances clearance, the section 4.3 ban on third-party financial products and economic-risk-limiting transactions, blacklisting, and section 5 notification.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; a subset of Designated Personnel with an additional, separate obligation under section 6 to notify the Company Secretary of trades within 3 days so the Company can make ASX Listing Rule notifications.

tiers.name: associates
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, dependent children, any trustee of a trust under which the person, spouse/partner or dependent children is a beneficiary, any company the person controls or holds a majority of shares in, and any other entity where the person is a director, secretary or executive officer (unless properly walled off from trading decisions).

definitions.hedging_definition: a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their securityholding in the Company

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release to ASX of the Company's annual results
windows.end_anchor: release to ASX of the Company's annual results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release to ASX of the Company's half yearly results
windows.end_anchor: release to ASX of the Company's half yearly results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: release of the Company's quarterly reports

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other period to be a Prohibited Period, and may at its discretion vary the rule for a particular Prohibited Period by general announcement to all Designated Personnel; confidentiality of such determinations is not addressed. The Board or Chairperson may also privately notify a Designated Person that they are subject to a blacklist on the securities of another entity (section 4.4).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on dealing in any financial product issued or created over the Securities by a third party, or dealing in associated products; no vesting-state carve-out, no clearance route, and none of the section 7 Exempt Transactions relieve it.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel are prohibited from dealing in any financial products issued or created over the Securities by third parties, or dealing in associated products.

rules.detail: For personnel who are not Designated Personnel, derivatives are only caught because Securities are defined to include them; dealing is permitted subject only to the general insider trading prohibition, since section 4.3 does not apply to this tier.
rules.evidence: Securities may include shares, options, derivatives, managed investment products, and any other financial products of the Company that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Freestanding, unconditional ban on any transaction limiting the economic risk of a Designated Person's securityholding, additional to and independent of the third-party financial product ban; no vesting-state distinction and no exemption listed.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their securityholding in the Company.

rules.detail: The section 4.3 hedging ban applies only to Designated Personnel; no hedging restriction is stated for other Group personnel.
A prepaid forward or similar monetisation structure is a financial product created over the Securities by a third party, and so is banned in the same terms as any other third-party derivative.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel are prohibited from dealing in any financial products issued or created over the Securities by third parties, or dealing in associated products.

rules.detail: Short selling of the Securities is expressly addressed, though drafted as 'should not' rather than 'must not'; non-compliance with the Policy generally is treated as serious misconduct.
rules.evidence: Additionally, employees and directors should not engage in short selling of the Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.
A CFD is a financial product created by a third party (the CFD provider) that references the Securities, and so falls squarely within the section 4.3 ban even though 'CFD' is not named.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel are prohibited from dealing in any financial products issued or created over the Securities by third parties, or dealing in associated products.

rules.detail: For non-Designated personnel, a CFD is only caught via the broad Securities/financial product definition and the general insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Securities may include shares, options, derivatives, managed investment products, and any other financial products of the Company that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on employees and directors entering margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities, justified by the risk of a forced sale while the person holds inside information; no clearance route or exemption stated.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities as the terms may require the Securities be sold when the employee or director possesses inside information.

rules.detail: Encumbrance is not separately named, but a margin lending arrangement necessarily involves using the Securities as collateral; the ban on margin lending is read to prohibit that encumbrance.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities as the terms may require the Securities be sold when the employee or director possesses inside information.

rules.detail: Only 'margin lending arrangements' are named (unlike some peer policies which also catch 'similar funding arrangements'); however the stated rationale, the risk of a forced sale while holding inside information, applies equally to any loan secured on the Securities, so a bank loan secured on collared shares would likely be treated as caught.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities as the terms may require the Securities be sold when the employee or director possesses inside information.

rules.detail: Trading in and out of Securities within 3 months, or speculative trading, should not occur; the Board may at its discretion exclude disposals of Employee Share Scheme securities from this restriction.
rules.evidence: they should not engage in short-term trading (that is, trading in and out of Securities over a period of 3 months or less) or speculative trading in the Securities.

clearance.approver: Relevant Officer (the Chairperson of the Board, or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee if the applicant is the Chairperson)
clearance.evidence: No dealing may be undertaken before the Designated Person receives written clearance from the Relevant Officer. If the Designated Person receives written clearance for their proposed dealing, that dealing must be completed within 7 days from the date of the clearance, unless it specifies otherwise.

clearance.approver: Relevant Officer (the Chairperson of the Board, or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee if the applicant is the Chairperson)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: confirmation given when the approved trading has been completed
clearance.evidence: If approval is granted in writing in accordance with this clause, the Designated Person must complete the dealing within 7 days of receiving such approval, or such earlier time as determined.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (for ASX Listing Rule notification)
clearance.evidence: Directors must notify the Company Secretary of any sale or purchase of the Securities within 3 days of such trade occurring so that the Company may notify ASX in compliance with the ASX Listing Rules.

short_term.basis: trading in and out of Securities
carve_outs: Board may, at its discretion, exclude the disposal by employees of Securities received under the Company's Employee Share Scheme from this restriction
short_term.evidence: they should not engage in short-term trading (that is, trading in and out of Securities over a period of 3 months or less) or speculative trading in the Securities.

exceptions.evidence: transfer of the Securities by a Designated Person to a person closely related to the Designated Person (e.g. spouse, family trust or related body corporate) or to their superannuation fund
disposal of the Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back
acquisition of the Securities under a pro rata issue
acquisition of the Securities under a security purchase plan or dividend reinvestment plan
acquisition of the Securities under an employee incentive scheme
any other transactions identified by the Board for this purpose

exceptions.approver: Relevant Officer (Chairperson of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: the person is experiencing severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances; after investigating all reasonable alternatives, the sale of the Securities is the only practical way of addressing the exceptional circumstances

exemption_authority: None beyond the Relevant Officer's exceptional-circumstances approval under 4.2 (severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances, sale the only practical remedy, and no inside information) and the Board's power to designate further Exempt Transactions under 7(f). The section 4.3 bans on third-party financial products and economic-risk-limiting transactions, and the section 3.2 margin lending ban, have no exemption or clearance route at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel are prohibited from dealing in any financial products issued or created over the Securities by third parties, or dealing in associated products.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This clause targets bank-structured products referencing the Company's shares directly; it independently and absolutely prohibits a Designated Person from entering an OTC put/call with a bank regardless of vesting state, with no listed exemption or clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their securityholding in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a freestanding hedging ban additional to the third-party product ban; it would independently catch the put/call legs of a collar even if structured as a bilateral contract rather than a 'financial product issued by a third party'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and directors are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities as the terms may require the Securities be sold when the employee or director possesses inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The stated rationale (forced-sale risk while holding inside information) is not conceptually limited to conventional margin lenders and would apply with equal force to a bank loan secured on the collared shares, so the ban should likely be read to extend to any securities-backed financing even though only 'margin lending' is named.

bespoke_clauses.clause: that dealing must be completed within 7 days from the date of the clearance, unless it specifies otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the ordinary clearance and the exceptional-circumstances approval require any permitted dealing to complete within 7 days of clearance, requiring tight coordination with the bank for any leg of a structure that is not itself independently banned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the Board or the Chairperson of the Board notifies a Designated Person in writing that they are subject to a blacklist in relation to the securities of a particular entity (Blacklisted Securities), that person must not deal in the Blacklisted Securities from the time period specified in the notice.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank counterparty itself, or a related entity, were ever the subject of a blacklist notice to the executive (e.g. due to a related transaction giving rise to inside information about the bank), dealing with that bank could be independently blocked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Non-compliance with this Policy will be considered as serious misconduct and may result in disciplinary action and/or termination of employment or engagement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Breach of the section 4.3 bans through a collar structure exposes the executive to disciplinary action including termination, independent of any separate insider trading liability.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a director or senior executive (Designated Personnel) under this policy. Section 4.3 imposes two independent, unconditional bans: dealing in any financial product issued or created over the Securities by a third party, and entering any transaction that limits the economic risk of the securityholding — both apply regardless of vesting state, have no clearance path, and are not relieved by any of the section 7 Exempt Transactions. The loan leg is separately blocked by the section 3.2 ban on margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities, which binds all employees and directors and is reasoned on a forced-sale-while-holding-inside-information rationale that would likely extend to any bank loan secured on the collared shares even though only 'margin lending' is named. Even setting aside sections 3.2 and 4.3, any dealing during a Prohibited Period (two weeks before annual, half-year or quarterly results, or as otherwise declared by the Board) needs prior written clearance from the Chairperson (or the Audit and Risk Committee Chair), must complete within 7 days, and Designated Personnel must give the Company Secretary written confirmation within 3 days of dealing. No exemption authority can override the section 3.2 or 4.3 bans; the only relief is the Board's power to designate further exempt transactions or the Chairperson's narrow exceptional-circumstances (severe hardship, sale-only) approval, neither of which accommodates a collar or its financing.
